question.problem: Calculate the second derivative of  $f(s)=⟨\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\operatorname{cos}⁡4s⟩$ with respect to $s.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the derivative of $f(s)$ by differentiating each component.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate ${f}^{″}(s)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4s⟩\end{aligned}
$$
